meta.title: Trust in politicians
meta.question: How much do Poles trust politicians?
meta.measure: Average trust in politicians, from 0 (no trust at all) to 10 (complete trust)
meta.anchor: Pooled from every question on trust or confidence in politicians and MPs, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Agree or disagree: it is better not to trust politicians
items.notes: CDCEE, January 1991 and March 2000. Binary; agreeing (distrust) is 0.

PGSW 2001 and 2005. 'Trust very much / rather trust / rather distrust / completely distrust'. MPs as people rather than parliament as an institution, so here and not in trust_parliament. The 2005 wave II repeat (trust_mps_w2, half the sample after the presidential election) is left out.

items.wording: Trust in politicians (0 no trust at all ... 10 complete trust)
items.notes: ESS Poland, rounds 1-11 (2002-2023), 11 surveys. Round 10 (2021-22) was self-completion; the pipeline's MODE_SPLITS makes it a question of its own.

items.wording: Do you trust MPs and senators? (definitely yes ... definitely no)
items.notes: CBOS, 2004-09 (APiW 172), 1 survey. One-off CBOS trust questions answered 'zdecydowanie tak ... zdecydowanie nie' (not the 'mam zaufanie' battery).

items.wording: Trust in politicians on an 11-point scale (1 complete lack of trust ... 11 full trust)
items.notes: CBOS, 2008-07 (APiW 218), 1 survey. 11-point card, 1 = complete lack of trust ... 11 = full trust (intermediate codes unlabelled).

items.wording: Most politicians are trustworthy (strongly agree ... strongly disagree)
items.notes: PGSW 2019, 1 survey. Also one of the Populist attitudes items (CSES module 5).

items.wording: Trust in politicians (0 no trust at all ... 10 complete trust)
items.notes: ESS round 10 (2021-22): self-completion by web and paper in Poland, where every other round was face to face, so a question of its own.
